license: MIT (repo LICENSE: 'The license of the original trained model can be found at https://github.com/w-hc/torch_audioset/blob/master/LICENSE'); weights are Google's YAMNet (Apache-2.0) ported to PyTorch by w-hc/torch_audioset
input: audio [1,1,96,64] = log-mel patch (0.96 s). The frontend is NOT in the graph; sound_classifier.py computes it in numpy with YAMNet's parameters (16 kHz, 25 ms Hann / 10 ms hop, 512 FFT, 64 HTK-mel 125-7500 Hz, log(mel+0.001))
output: class_scores [1,521] = LOGITS; sigmoid gives YAMNet's scores
frontend_check: 2026-09-23: sigmoid(this model on our numpy log-mel) matched Google's own graph (zeropointnine/yamnet-onnx, tf2onnx of the official Kaggle model, sha256 1510041d...8e19) to within ~0.02 on every test window, e.g. Cap gun 0.894 vs 0.89, Gunshot 0.78 vs 0.78
